accuracy.note: On fictional test data, 19 Nov 2026. The clean set covers 31 of the 32 agents: menu engineering sorts every dish into a group, so a menu with no labels does not exist. This pass also found and fixed one wrong finding on the demo data and five wrong or noisy results on public data.

real_data: NYC Department of Health, Restaurant Inspection Results (one ZIP code, 2024 to Nov 2026)
NYC Open Data, public; NYC Open Data terms of use

fairtable-health-inspections on 1,758 inspections at 648 restaurants (5,479 published rows, one per violation, grouped into one row per inspection). It showed four problems, now fixed: NYC scores count violation points (lower is better), NYC names routine visits Cycle Inspection, same-day records changed the result, and critical violations after a passing visit were reported as open (now a follow-up score setting). After the fixes, 0 disagreements in 499 checks against an independent re-count from the same rows. Tested from one year earlier, routine-due had flagged 36 of the 48 restaurants inspected in the next 45 days, and 57 of its 199 flags were inspected within 90 days.
U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics average retail prices, 8 food items, via FRED
BLS data, public domain; served by FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

fairtable-price-creep on the last 13 monthly prices of each item, written as invoice lines. Price rises over 5% were reported for ground beef (+6.8%) and tomatoes (+9.1%), as the series show. The steady-creep rule was too noisy: it fired for 7 of 8 items, including items that ended cheaper. It now needs a current run of rises that adds up to 5%, and fires once (eggs, up three months running). 0 disagreements with an independent re-check.

human_review: Food cost pack
A manager checks each flagged ingredient against the count sheet, recipe and invoices, then decides whether to recount, retrain, or change a recipe or vendor.
Bar and menu pack
The bar manager decides whether a pour gap is over-pouring, unrung drinks or a count error; menu and price changes are the owner's call.
Front of house and cash pack
A manager talks through each void, comp and drawer short with the staff member, and a person decides on any no-show fee, refund or gift card correction.
Labor pack
The owner or payroll provider checks wage, tip, overtime and break findings against your state's current rules and payroll records; the agents never run payroll.
Delivery apps and fees pack
Someone disputes commissions, error charges and card fees in each platform's portal or with the processor; a draft letter is sent only by a person.
Back office pack
The bookkeeper confirms tax rates and returns and decides which possible duplicate invoices to hold; nothing is paid or filed by the agents.
Compliance calendar pack
A manager books service visits, renews permits and certificates and confirms allergen labels with the kitchen; intervals and rules come from your own jurisdiction.
Whole restaurant
Every finding in every pack goes to a named person, who looks and acts; the agents only read files and write reports and drafts.
Small group
Each location manager reviews their own findings; the owner or operations lead reviews how each location compares with the group median.
Partner rollout
Each location's manager acts on its findings, and the firm or head office confirms each location's settings (wage, tax and inspection rules) with the client.
common_problems: Ingredients used well beyond what the recipes and sales say (chicken breast 27% over in the demo week).
Vendor prices above the bid sheet, and cases that got smaller at the same case price.
Short or refused deliveries with no credit memo.
A bartender's drawer short four nights running, and a deposit that does not match the count.
Voids approved by the server who rang them, and comps over the limit with no approver.
Delivery orders charged more commission than the contract, error charges, and orders never paid.
Tip credit shortfalls, where cash wage plus tips fell under the minimum set for your state.
Expired or expiring permits and certificates, and hood or fire suppression service past due.
reaches_the_model: When an assistant calls a tool, its model sees the result: totals, findings, amounts, quantities, dates, rates and finding codes in clear. It also sees text such as item, recipe and vendor names, locations, and free-text reasons and notes exactly as they were typed. Staff, guest and client names, phone numbers, emails, employee IDs, gift card numbers and certificate numbers are replaced by tokens such as A.R.#3f9a2c or card#7ecbb1 (checked with 118 fictional values in 14 agents, 0 leaks). The report and draft files written on your computer keep the real values. Results go to whatever model your assistant uses; for staff pay and schedule data, use a model covered by your own agreements or a local model.
rules_maintained: Every rule that changes with the law or a contract is a setting, not code: the minimum and tipped cash wage, overtime and break rules, minors' hours, sales tax rates, marketplace channels, the allergen list, food handler grace periods, inspection and equipment intervals, card fee caps and delivery commission rates. Defaults live in each agent's src/logic.js, with the source named in the review. Your own values go in a settings JSON file that is merged over the defaults, and every result lists the settings it used. You change the file yourself, or support updates it when a rate or rule changes.
